title: Affine coherent edge isomorphisms compatible with base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $K=Rf_*(G[0])$ in $D(\mathcal O_S)$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image] and $A=H^0(K)$, $E=H^1(K)$. Assume $A,E$ are finite locally free [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], $K$ is Zariski-locally isomorphic to $A[0]\oplus E[-1]$, and for every scheme morphism $g:T\to S$ the canonical module base-change map $\delta_g:Lg^*K\to Rf_{T,*}(G_T[0])$ [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map] is an isomorphism. Here $X_T=X\times_ST$, $f_T:X_T\to T$, $j_T:X_T\to X$, $G_T=j_T^*G$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback]; $E[-1]$ places $E$ in cohomological degree one. Let $\tau:K\to E[-1]$ be the canonical truncation morphism inducing the identity on $H^1$. The map $\gamma_g=H^1(Lg^*\tau):H^1(Lg^*K)\to g^*E$ [def-pc-derived-pullback] is invertible. Write $\beta_g=H^1(\delta_g)\gamma_g^{-1}:g^*E\to R^1f_{T,*}G_T$. For every affine $T$ and $g:T\to S$, the canonical Leray edge $\varepsilon_T:H^1(X_T,G_T)\to\Gamma(T,R^1f_{T,*}G_T)$ [lem-pc-leray-degenerate-sections, pqf-def-cohomology] is invertible, and
$$e_g=\Gamma(T,\beta_g^{-1})\varepsilon_T:H^1(X_T,G_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,g^*E)$$
is $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-linear. These maps are simultaneous and compatible with every $S$-morphism $h:T'\to T$ between affine base schemes:
$$e_{gh}\circ h_X^*=\rho_h\circ e_g.$$
Here $h_X:X_{T'}\to X_T$, its coefficient morphism is the canonical $h_X^*G_T\cong G_{T'}$, and $h_X^*$ is the resulting module cohomology map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]; $\rho_h$ is section pullback followed by $h^*g^*E\cong(gh)^*E$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 0ATM, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; Tag 01FB, remark-explain-arrow; Tag 01F8, lemma-functoriality; Tag 01F2, lemma-Leray. Application of these constructions to a two-degree locally free derived direct image.

proof.text: Put $K_g=Rf_{T,*}(G_T[0])$. Choose an open cover $(V_i)$ of $S$ on which $K|_{V_i}\cong A|_{V_i}[0]\oplus E|_{V_i}[-1]$ and both modules are finite free. A free module is flat: tensoring with $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ is a finite direct sum of identity functors, hence preserves kernels and cokernels. Thus this two-term zero-differential model is a bounded-above complex of flat modules, hence K-flat by the bounded-above flat lemma. Put $T_i=g^{-1}(V_i)$ and let $g_i:T_i\to V_i$ be the restricted morphism. The open-restriction lemma for derived pullback gives $(Lg^*K)|_{T_i}\cong Lg_i^*(K|_{V_i})$, and since derived pullback is computed termwise on a K-flat complex, $Lg_i^*(K|_{V_i})\cong g_i^*A[0]\oplus g_i^*E[-1]$ with finite free terms. Use the assumed isomorphism $\delta_g$ to compute the cohomology sheaves of $K_g$ on each $T_i$ (cohomology sheaves commute with restriction to opens). They are finite free in degrees zero and one and zero otherwise. In particular $K_g$ has no cohomology above one and each $R^qf_{T,*}G_T$ is quasi-coherent: locally it is a tilde of a finite free module, or zero. This reasoning applies to every $g$, with no flatness condition on $g$.

source.place: Tag 06YD, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; derived pullback local K-flat construction; application of the assumed local splitting and delta_g

proof.text: Apply the top-cohomology comparison with $n=1$ to $K$. Its specified truncation projection is exactly $\tau$ in the statement, so $\gamma_g=\kappa_{g,K}$, including the canonical identification $H^1(Lg^*E[-1])=g^*E$. Hence $\gamma_g$ is invertible; $H^1(\delta_g)$ is invertible by hypothesis, and $\beta_g=H^1(\delta_g)\kappa_{g,K}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_T$-modules.

source.place: Tag 05TC, dual truncation argument; the canonical top comparison applied in degree one

proof.text: If $T$ is affine, the quasi-coherence in Step 1 gives $H^p(T,R^qf_{T,*}G_T)=0$ for every $p>0$ and $q\geq0$ by affine vanishing. The degenerate Leray theorem therefore makes its cocycle-defined $\varepsilon_T$ invertible. Its cocycle formula agrees with $\theta_T$ in the higher-direct-image presheaf theorem: both send a section cocycle of $f_{T,*}I^\bullet$ to its image in the cohomology sheaf. That theorem gives a morphism of presheaves of modules, so this map is $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-linear. The section map of the module isomorphism $\beta_g^{-1}$ is linear too. Their composite $e_g$ is consequently a linear isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 01F4(2) and 01E4, respective cocycle descriptions; affine vanishing Tag 01EO

proof.text:
Fix $h:T'\to T$ over $S$, and write $m_h:Lh^*K_g\to K_{gh}$ for the canonical module base-change map for $(f_T,h,G_T)$, with coefficient identified by $h_X^*G_T\cong G_{gh}$. The derived-to-ordinary single-module comparisons $c_a$ of the module base-change definition (the value at $M[0]$ of the left-derived counit, followed by the single-complex identification) satisfy, for $w:X_{T'}\to X_T$, $v:X_T\to X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$, $c_{vw,M}\circ\mathrm{comp}=c^{\rm ord}\circ c_{w,v^*M}\circ Lw^*(c_{v,M})$, where $\mathrm{comp}:Lw^*Lv^*\cong L(vw)^*$ is the canonical derived composition isomorphism and $c^{\rm ord}:w^*v^*M\cong(vw)^*M$ the ordinary one; this is exactly the canonical single-pullback composition lemma with $f=w$, $g=v$, $N=M$, and needs no flatness. Now apply derived horizontal pasting to the squares $(f,f_T,g,v)$ and $(f_T,f_{T'},h,w)$ at $E=G[0]$, then naturality of the second mate in its coefficient along $c_{v,G}:Lv^*(G[0])\to(v^*G)[0]$, and finally the displayed identity: the inverse composition isomorphism $c(t,p)^{-1}$ produced by pasting cancels against $\mathrm{comp}$. After the canonical fibre-product and pullback identifications, it gives
$$\delta_{gh}=m_h\circ Lh^*(\delta_g):Lh^*Lg^*K\longrightarrow K_{gh}.$$
This is an equality of the specified maps, not a choice of an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0ATM, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, with remark-base-change; composition of the derived-to-ordinary single-module comparisons

proof.text:
Let $F_g=H^1(K_g)$ and put $b_h=H^1(m_h)\kappa_{h,K_g}^{-1}:h^*F_g\to F_{gh}$, which is defined since Step 1 gives $K_g\in D^{\leq1}$. Naturality of $\kappa$ at $\delta_g:Lg^*K\to K_g$ gives
$$\kappa_{h,K_g}H^1(Lh^*\delta_g)=h^*H^1(\delta_g)\kappa_{h,Lg^*K}.$$
The composition formula gives $\kappa_{gh,K}=c^{\rm ord}_{g,h,E}\,h^*\kappa_{g,K}\,\kappa_{h,Lg^*K}$. Combining these two equations with Step 4, and substituting the definitions of $\beta_g$ and $b_h$, yields
$$\beta_{gh}\,c^{\rm ord}_{g,h,E}=b_h\,h^*\beta_g.$$
Every factor in the substitution has the indicated source and target; in particular no inverse of $m_h$ is used.

source.place: Tag 05TC, natural top comparison; composition and naturality applied to delta_g

proof.text:
Apply the top-degree derived/presheaf comparison to $f_T$, $h$, $G_T$, $q=1$. Its upper-vanishing hypothesis holds by Step 1 and its $b_h^1$ is precisely $b_h$ of Step 5. At the whole open $T$, its cocycle maps are $\varepsilon_T$ and $\varepsilon_{T'}$ by Step 3. If $s_h(F):\Gamma(T,F)\to\Gamma(T',h^*F)$ is the section map of the ordinary pullback unit, its adjunction formula therefore reads
$$\varepsilon_{T'}h_X^*=\Gamma(T',b_h)\,s_h(F_g)\,\varepsilon_T.$$
The coefficient on the left is exactly the canonical $h_X^*G_T\cong G_{gh}$ used in the statement; thus this is the required module cohomology pullback, without an etale or underlying-abelian comparison.

source.place: Tag 01E4, cocycle sheafification applied to the whole open; the derived-mate/presheaf comparison

proof.text:
For a class $x\in H^1(X_T,G_T)$, substitute the last equation and Step 5 into the definition of $e_{gh}$. The result is
$$e_{gh}(h_X^*x)=\Gamma(T',c^{\rm ord}_{g,h,E})\,\Gamma(T',h^*\beta_g^{-1})\,s_h(F_g)(\varepsilon_Tx).$$
Naturality of the ordinary pullback unit changes the middle two factors to $s_h(g^*E)\,\Gamma(T,\beta_g^{-1})$. The whole expression is therefore $\rho_h(e_gx)$, as asserted. All maps were defined by canonical truncation, mate, section, and cocycle maps; the local splittings were used only to verify hypotheses. Consequently one simultaneous family $e_g$ works for every affine $g$ and every arrow $h$.

Two citation faults, both fixed in the item. (1) C1/C4, step 1: lem-sc-local-kflat-pullback-model needs the whole morphism T to factor through the open, which a general g does not, and the restriction (Lg^*K)|_{g^{-1}V_i} = Lg_i^*(K|_{V_i}) was not cited. The step now cites lem-pc-derived-pullback-open-restriction-universes and def-pc-derived-pullback (termwise on the K-flat free model). (2) C1/C5, step 4: the identity c_{vw}=c_w Lw^*(c_v) was proved by transposing, which needs the derived composition isomorphism to be compatible with the adjunctions, and no cited node states that. The existing node lem-pc-canonical-single-pullback-composition states the identity itself, so the step now cites it and spells out the pasting and cancellation. Steps 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are correct: I redid the beta algebra of step 5 and the unit-naturality cancellation of step 7, and in step 3 the cocycle maps eps and theta are the same map, which gives linearity. New nodes are kept. lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology is true: Lg^* is right t-exact, and the n=0 case Spec F_p -> Spec Z (Tor in degree -1), C=0 and empty T all check; no duplicate found. lem-weil-pbc-top-base-change-presheaf is true by reducing to the ordinary adjoint through tau_{>=q} and naturality of theta; no duplicate (the flat-sections node assumes flatness).
